subject.title: refactor: move non-session runtime journals to SQLite

question: Should file-based audit and ACP diagnostic access be retired only after every platform writer and documented consumer has an equivalent SQLite-backed access path?
rationale: The PR removes a documented response field and operator-visible file paths while changing persisted diagnostic storage, so the permanent compatibility contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve access before merge
options.body: Add supported SQLite-backed inspection or export paths, migrate every remaining writer and consumer, and prove upgrades before retiring the files.

options.title: Accept the breaking retirement
options.body: Explicitly approve removal of the file handles and document the operator and integration consequences as an intentional compatibility change.

options.title: Split incomplete surfaces
options.body: Land only migrations with complete writer, reader, documentation, and upgrade coverage, leaving ACP or macOS audit storage for follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Preserve access before merge
recommendation.body: Add supported SQLite-backed inspection or export paths, migrate every remaining writer and consumer, and prove upgrades before retiring the files.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged session/transcript SQLite flip provides the closest established architecture and migration precedent available in the item context.
